restrictions: Target sha256-r38-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..37 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words; outputs two distinct 128-byte messages M0 || M1, M0 || M1' with equal digests.

Construction: the memory-efficient A0-variant attack (design of 2d1c4fc2 and fb176310 on ePrint 2026/1120 / 2026/1080), our implementation experiments/a0p38.py, with our characteristic P8 and the accepted event rows 16..22 (row 19 on signed differences) plus a direct output comparison.

Cost: exact ledger ledger_a0p.py: N_FB = 6,005,607,090,201,049,622,085,684 first blocks, 8 classes of 24,576 variants, the row-16 program of 1511 instructions per 256 variants, executed counts; T x 2728 = 492898079323702689657340761015; claimed 87.22358.
Success probability at least 0.39 under H1, H2 (q3_model 2^-97.0000), H3, by Bonferroni per first block, independent first blocks and Chebyshev caps.
Memory 2^28.10 bytes (online 608,864 bytes; the preprocessing peak).

heuristics.statement: For M0 uniform on {0,1}^512 (two fresh random words per first block), CV1 = F_38(IV, M0) behaves as a uniform 256-bit value for the events of one fixed variant (W7, W16..W22 and E16x distributed as in Lemma 5.1).
heuristics.scope: g, the per-first-block success probability and the expected work.
heuristics.extrapolation: The premise of the A0-variant lineage; the organizer experiment a0p-online-r38 runs the program on real first blocks.
heuristics.limitations: A premise about the first-block compression.

heuristics.statement: The average over the 196,608 selected variants of Pr[the pair is in the accepted event (rows 16..22 with row 19 on signed differences, equal outputs) | good pair] is at least q3_model = 2^-97.0000.
heuristics.scope: N_FB and the whole attack term.
heuristics.extrapolation: 20 multilevel-splitting runs (C) with the variants of the selected classes: mean 2^-96.3683, one-sided 99% Student bound 2^-96.9759, bootstrap 2^-96.8088, 89,254 verified collisions (one stalled run counted as 0); an independent Python implementation (the organizer replica, a lower-bound event restricted to four row-19 patterns and 512 sampled variants): 480 development replicates, mean 2^-96.2992; organizer replica a0p-q3-r38 with a frozen pass rule.
heuristics.limitations: Participant-run Monte Carlo with a heavy-tailed row-20 stage; the replica tests a reduced version.

heuristics.statement: The average over successes of the expected number of other row-16 passes of the same first block is at most 2^-5.9.
heuristics.scope: The Bonferroni factor of a first block.
heuristics.extrapolation: 750 rebuilt successes: 2 other row-16 passes among 36,741,120 evaluated variants of the passing classes; 99% Poisson limit 2^-6.48.

heuristics.statement: The computation spent on the characteristic search, S and the class data, and all development is at most A_C + A_S + DEV = 2^48 + 2^50 + 2^50 target compressions.
heuristics.extrapolation: One 10-core machine, less than 2^21 core-seconds in all; holds at up to 2^27 compressions per core-second.
heuristics.limitations: Wall-clock bound; A_C up to 2^84 changes the claim by less than 0.003.

heuristics.statement: One instruction on a 256-bit plane costs one word operation (the 256-bit word RAM of the cost model); the row-16 program is charged at its executed instruction count, loads and stores included.
heuristics.extrapolation: Executed instruction by instruction and compared with the scalar definition on sampled batches (selftest, a0p-online-r38).
